figures.question: Where do the reflected first pulse and incoming second pulse overlap?
figures.reading: Both packets begin outside r=14. Central reflection sends the first outward through the second incoming packet.
figures.significance: This supplies opposite radial directions and allows both-minus-each-alone subtraction.
figures.limitation: The left panel removes the 1/r focusing factor. The right uses symmetric log color; this is not two planar beams.
transformations: base grid; reshape time/radius rows; multiply a by r to expose radial transport; signed contraction uses symmetric log normalization with linear threshold 0.001 of its maximum absolute value; show t<=55

figures.question: Do locally triggered intervals carry a resolved predicted clock record?
figures.reading: Local marker check: fail; resolution: pass; interval prediction: fail.
figures.significance: The interval uses locally recorded neutral events and local clock quadrature, rather than coordinate arrival alone.
figures.limitation: The quiet history is evaluated at counterfactual event times. Last-fall selection is retrospective in a finite window.
transformations: local atan2 phase from chi and chi_dot; quiet subtraction; first/last absolute-a threshold crossings

figures.question: Does surface-only prediction match the withheld local clock and density response?
figures.significance: This tests the neutral-to-core-to-clock coefficient without fitting the withheld evolution.
figures.limitation: The Taylor and full evolutions share the discrete Hamiltonian. Agreement is bounded by independent numerical controls.
transformations: finer grid h=.025; matched quiet subtraction; multiply Taylor coefficients by A squared

figures.question: Is the local record larger than independent numerical errors?
figures.reading: Bars compare absolute interval magnitude, direct numerical error and prediction residual. Resolution requires signal greater than five error budgets.
figures.significance: A good-looking trace cannot substitute for a resolved local interval.
figures.limitation: The budget is deterministic, not a statistical confidence interval. The finest profile is interpolated, not independently re-solved.
transformations: absolute values; log floor1e-16; budgets from finer/fine + base/time + base/wide +1e-11 cycles

figures.question: Do sign, amplitude, pulse-overlap and clock-phase controls support the response mechanism?
figures.reading: Weak amplitude exponent 1.999370; overlap check pass; frozen-core control pass.
figures.significance: Individual pulses isolate the interaction term; clock phase changes test a held-out response configuration.
figures.limitation: Sign symmetry is enforced by the action and is not independent evidence for the response coefficient.
transformations: divide amplitude traces by A squared; half-sum/difference; both-minus-single-minus-second; h=.025

figures.question: Can the upstream record distinguish incoming drive from returning radiation?
figures.reading: Incoming and outgoing characteristics are built from a, a_t and a_r. Only t=0..16 is inverted.
figures.significance: The predictor no longer consumes the prescribed interior neutral history.
figures.limitation: This is a linear acquisition on a frozen core. Exterior vacuum inversion has mesh and tail errors.
